It's not documented but if you make one request with event functions, the Lambda runtime lives for about 7 minutes before it's reaped. If you have a lot of rarely invoked functions, it is cheaper to use Lambda Event Functions. There you'll pay for GB/s for the duration of your function. jobs.text: Those fucking rent-seeking hyperscalers took the internet away from you, and we’re going to give it back to you and to everyone. We’re distilling out the good parts, and we’re building the connective tissue that draws them together. 100% of the internet is going to be open source soon, and we’re going to force it open. Loudly. Hell yeah. Our organization is flat, and we're going to go after everybody and everything. Everything you build here will be open source. We have no private repos. We can reclaim the internet. That’s our mission. Want to know more about us? Look up “Adobe ArtCraft” on YouTube / TikTok / your platform of choice. quantaArticles.title: A New Era for the Dawn of Life
quantaArticles.description: Creative, interdisciplinary, and bold, the study of the origins of life has entered a new age. Welcome to Quanta Magazine’s special series on the origins of life.
quantaArticles.author: Yasemin Saplakoglu, Philip Ball, Perri Thaler and Jake Buehler

quantaArticles.title: The Evolving Story of How Chemistry Became Biology
quantaArticles.description: After decades of bickering about which molecules came first, a new generation of scientists is rethinking what life was, is, and could be.
quantaArticles.author: Yasemin Saplakoglu

quantaArticles.title: How a Metabolic Spark Could Have Jump-Started Life
quantaArticles.description: Energetic pathways that make and break complex molecules are critical to all life. It’s even possible that these self-sustaining cycles could have been key at life’s beginning.
quantaArticles.author: Jake Buehler

quantaArticles.title: The Case for a Bubble at Life’s Start
quantaArticles.description: Is self-enclosure life’s greatest trick? According to the lipid-first theory, a cell membrane enabled life by giving chemistry a place to gather.
quantaArticles.author: Perri Thaler

quantaArticles.title: Did Life Begin in an RNA World?
quantaArticles.description: Some believe the earliest life emerged from self-copying molecules that could mutate and even evolve. But that may not have been enough.
quantaArticles.author: Philip Ball

infoqArticles.title: Technical Debt is Social; it is the Price of Learning by Doing
infoqArticles.description: Technical debt is not necessarily a sign of poor engineering. It can be the price of learning through software in use. As AI accelerates code production beyond our capacity to understand code and context, technical debt increasingly becomes a sociotechnical challenge. By Ben Linders
infoqArticles.author: Ben Linders

infoqArticles.title: Presentation: Opening the Black Box: Critical Explainability for AI Agent Tool Selection with Kiji Inspector
infoqArticles.description: Hannes Hapke shares how Dataiku’s open-source Kiji Inspector applies Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) directly to decision tokens to expose why agents pick specific tools. Moving past superficial chain-of-thought narratives, he discusses causal ablation, layer activation extraction via patched vLLM engines, and production monitoring workflows for software architects and senior engineering leaders. By Ha
infoqArticles.author: Hannes Hapke

infoqArticles.title: Azure Logic Apps Standard Gets a Local CLI in Preview
infoqArticles.description: Microsoft has released a public preview of the logicapp extension for the Azure CLI, adding local project creation, workflow authoring, a runtime lifecycle, connector management, run inspection, and test scaffolding for Logic Apps Standard, work that previously required the VS Code extension. The product team pitches the terminal surface as determinism for AI-assisted development. By Steef-Jan Wig
infoqArticles.author: Steef-Jan Wiggers

infoqArticles.title: Google Open-Sources TPU Sync for KV Cache and Weight Transfer on TPUs
infoqArticles.description: Google Cloud has open-sourced TPU Sync, a native C++ library that moves KV cache blocks and model weights between TPU HBM, host DRAM, shared storage, and the data center network. By Daniel Dominguez
infoqArticles.author: Daniel Dominguez

infoqArticles.title: Author Q+A: finprim is a Case for One Financial Validation Library in TypeScript
infoqArticles.description: finprim is an MIT-licensed TypeScript library that offers IBAN, BIC, card, sort code, VAT, routing number and loan functions through one API with no runtime dependencies. Its author built it after duplicated validators drifted apart across web and mobile. It validates and formats data only, and does not process payments. He is cautious about adding SEPA and ACH file generation. By Daniel Curtis
infoqArticles.author: Daniel Curtis

infoqArticles.title: LinkedIn Replaces Argo CD with a Custom GitOps Engine for Kubernetes Deployments
infoqArticles.description: In a recent post, LinkedIn revealed it has replaced Argo CD with its own GitOps engine. This new system deploys applications across over 250 Kubernetes clusters. It supports more than 4,000 services and manages over 100,000 deployments each week. By Claudio Masolo
infoqArticles.author: Claudio Masolo

infoqArticles.title: GitHub Makes Agentic Workflows Generally Available with Isolation and Budget Controls
infoqArticles.description: GitHub Agentic Workflows is generally available, running coding agents in GitHub Actions with read-only defaults and separately scoped write jobs. Those protections do not cover direct write permissions or custom jobs, so they depend on how each workflow is configured. By Mark Silvester
infoqArticles.author: Mark Silvester

infoqArticles.title: JioHotstar Benchmarks Knowledge Bases for AI Coding Agents
infoqArticles.description: JioHotstar evaluated 6 approaches to code retrieval for AI coding agents using SWE, CodeScale Bench, and an internal question-answering harness. Structural search performed well on concrete tasks, while semantic retrieval helped with ambiguous requirements. The findings highlight trade-offs in accuracy, token use, and tool design, underscoring the need to match retrieval tools to task types. By Le
infoqArticles.author: Leela Kumili

infoqArticles.title: How LinkedIn, Netflix & DoorDash Run Agents, Evals & Inference in Production: QCon AI New York 2026
infoqArticles.description: QCon AI New York has published its full program for December 15–16, 2026. Engineers from LinkedIn, Netflix, DoorDash, Figma, Pinterest, Honeycomb, Harvey, Google DeepMind and OpenAI describe AI systems they run in production. Talks cover agent permissions and guardrails, eval loops, inference cost, AI code review, and team adoption. By Artenisa Chatziou
infoqArticles.author: Artenisa Chatziou

infoqArticles.title: Presentation: Uncorking Queueing Bottlenecks with OpenTelemetry
infoqArticles.description: Oli Lane and Julian Wreford share how Gearset replaced guesswork in distributed asynchronous queues with OpenTelemetry tracing. They explain why traditional metrics fall short, how to implement user-centric SLOs based on latency distributions, and share practical debugging tips to help senior developers, software architects, and engineering leaders improve system reliability and team culture. By J
infoqArticles.author: Julian Wreford, Oli Lane

infoqArticles.title: Article: The iOS Crash We Could Not Reproduce
infoqArticles.description: This article describes the investigation to find the root cause of a production crash in a large-scale iOS consumer app that had no clean stack trace. The crash occurred intermittently and resisted every local reproduction attempt. The final code change was small, but identifying the root cause required turning a vague SIGBUS report into a controlled set of experiments. By Abhishek Gang Deb
infoqArticles.author: Abhishek Gang Deb

infoqArticles.title: Angular's TypeScript 7-Powered Compiler Enters Beta with Rust-Based Preprocessor
infoqArticles.description: The Angular team has introduced ngp, a compiler preprocessor that rewrites the analysis stage in Rust using Oxc. It replaces ngc's dependence on the Transformer API, which TypeScript 7.0 removed. An early benchmark showed 2x to 3x faster cold builds. Adoption is expected in an Angular 22 minor release; production builds should stay on ngc until then. By Daniel Curtis
infoqArticles.author: Daniel Curtis

infoqArticles.title: Cloudflare Makes Basin Serverless Analytics Generally Available
infoqArticles.description: Cloudflare has announced the general availability of Basin, a serverless analytics platform built on Apache Iceberg and R2 Object Storage. The managed service supports open data formats and integrates with tools such as DuckDB, Snowflake, and Apache Spark, with no data egress fees. By Renato Losio
infoqArticles.author: Renato Losio

infoqArticles.title: Google Finds That Technical Debt Can Derail Coding Agents through "Agent Distraction"
infoqArticles.description: In a recent article, Google senior staff software engineer Sam Saccone and senior staff data scientist Madhuri Garikapati highlighted the cost of agent distraction, where AI coding agents get derailed by stale technical debt, such as old TODO comments, obsolete bug references, and outdated specs, leading them to embark on unrequested "side-quests". By Sergio De Simone
infoqArticles.author: Sergio De Simone

infoqArticles.title: Pinterest and Intel Take Open-Source Profiling to Internet Scale
infoqArticles.description: Pinterest has partnered with Intel to extend gProfiler, an open-source continuous profiler that provides production performance visibility across an internet-scale fleet of infrastructure. By Craig Risi
